newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama to propose regional distribution center.
newsitem.headline: Panama to propose regional distribution center.

text.p: Panama is expected to propose a regional distribution center for Pacific Rim countries during a two-day visit by Philippine President Fidel Ramos, a government spokesman said Monday.
"It is a Panamanian proposal to create a type of free-trade zone for APEC countries to distribute their products to Latin America from Panama," a Commerce Ministry spokesman said.
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, APEC, groups 18 nations, representing the Asian Pacific Rim plus Canada, Chile, Mexico and the United States.
Panama is keen to broaden ties with the Asia-Pacific and will use Ramos' visit to boost trade with the region.
Ramos, who arrives Tuesday accompanied by a 200-person delegation, is expected to meet privately with President Ernesto Perez Balladares and sign various accords.

The distribution center would form part of "Panama's plan to be more competitive in shipping. The privatization of the two ports and railroad will make us an important trans-shipment point for the Western Hemisphere," he said.
Panama recently partially privatized its two main ports and only railroad.
Ramos will also discuss investment opportunities in U.S. military installations that are scheduled to be turned over to Panamanian control in 1999.
